note.effort: Each minute of heart rate counts by the zone it falls in (Edwards TRIMP) and the total is mapped onto the 0 to 21 scale. It relies on your max heart rate, so set it in your profile for best results.
note.load: Load is the Edwards TRIMP: minutes in each heart rate zone multiplied by the zone number. The last 7 days add up to this workout; the weekly average is the mean of the 28 days before it.
note.threshold: Threshold pace is estimated from your best 1 mile, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon efforts over all your runs of the last 90 days (walks and hikes do not count), slowed to a one hour effort. It does not slow down just because your latest runs were easy. Zones are set as shares of it.

dynamics.title: Running dynamics
dynamics.how: Where do these numbers come from?
dynamics.explain: The watch sends these while you run, and JoyoFit averages them per minute. They only show when your watch sends them. For workouts synced before this feature, the figures can be fetched again from the watch for as long as it still holds them. Balance: the first figure is the left side as the watch sends it; we have not matched it against Huawei Health yet.

effect.title: Training effect
effect.explainWatch: Figures from the watch are what the watch reported after this workout, as is. Training effect runs from 0 to 5. We have not confirmed the units of the watch training points and load, and the watch load is not TRIMP. VO2max from the watch is rounded down to a whole number; values outside 10 to 90 are not shown.
effect.explainEstimate: Figures from the watch are what the watch reported after this workout, as is. Training effect runs from 0 to 5. The watch did not report an aerobic effect, so this is a JoyoFit estimate from the TRIMP of this workout: 5 x (1 - e^(-TRIMP / 150)). We have not confirmed the units of the watch training points and load, and the watch load is not TRIMP. VO2max from the watch is rounded down to a whole number; values outside 10 to 90 are not shown.

burn.title: Fat and carbs burned
burn.explain: An estimate by JoyoFit, the watch does not measure it: the {{kcal}} kcal are split over the time you actually spent at each heart rate, with a maximum of {{maxHr}} bpm (from HR zones in Settings, 220 minus your age by default). Easier effort burns a larger share of fat.

setup.gnssWhyBody: Huawei watches only get GPS assistance data from Huawei Health. JoyoFit sends your phone's location and time to help the first fix. Nothing is wrong with the watch.

location.title: Precise location
location.body: Route, distance and pace come from the phone's GPS. Your location is only used while you record a workout.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.body: Used to connect the heart rate strap and other sensors you paired.
bluetooth.denied: Bluetooth is not allowed yet, so your sensors will not connect. You can still record without sensors, or open settings to allow it.

steps.title: Count steps and cadence from the phone
steps.body: Optional. The phone's step counter gives the cadence and step count of a run, walk or hike when the phone is in a pocket, in your hand or in an armband. Nothing leaves the phone. You can start without this permission.
steps.denied: Step counter access is not allowed yet, so this recording has no cadence or steps from the phone. It still records. Open settings if you want to allow it.

gps.weak: Weak GPS signal, accuracy {{meters}} m. Find a more open spot.

ready.hintNoGps: Press Start when you are ready.
ready.noPhoneSteps: The phone step counter is off, so cadence and steps are only recorded when a running pod is connected.
ready.noService: A dark screen can stop the recording. Allow notifications and turn off battery saver for JoyoFit in the phone's settings so it keeps running.

refetch.bulkHint: For runs synced before running dynamics were kept: JoyoFit asks the watch to send their data again, only for the ones still on the watch. Only the dynamics figures are added, nothing else changes.

zones.hrNote: Zones follow your heart-rate zones as set now, also for past workouts. By default there are five, at 50-60, 60-70, 70-80, 80-90 and 90-100 percent of max heart rate; with the heart rate reserve method there are six, as on the watch (warm-up from 50 percent of the reserve, then basic aerobic and so on). Percentages are shares of the time spent in a zone. Strain does not use these zones: it always counts fixed percentages of max heart rate.
